title: 3Sum → 3Sum closest
label: ag-multi
statement: Return every **unique** triplet `(a, b, c)` from the array with `a + b + c == 0`. Each triplet ascending; the list in ascending order.
provenance: 3Sum is reported in an Agoda onsite (May 2026, FastPrep) and scores 75.6% on CodeJeet. Stage 2 is the standard companion (LeetCode 16).

stages.title: Zero-sum triplets
stages.say: Find all unique triplets that sum to zero.

stages.title: Closest to a target
stages.say: Now there may be no exact match. Return the sum of three numbers closest to a target.
stages.require: Add `ThreeSum.Closest(nums, target)` (long); ties go to the smaller sum; fewer than three numbers → `ArgumentException`.
testNames: tie goes to the smaller sum

prompts.label: Check my design — no code
prompts.text: I believe sort once, fix the first element, and close two pointers from both ends of the rest — O(n²) with duplicates skipped at every pointer so each triplet is produced once. Review my reasoning without giving me the implementation. What would break it?

prompts.label: Review, do not rewrite
prompts.text: Review my implementation for correctness and edge cases. Do not rewrite the code. List problems most severe first, each with the input that triggers it.

prompts.label: Race conditions
prompts.text: Now review this implementation for race conditions if multiple threads call ZeroTriplets concurrently. For each race, give the interleaving that breaks it. Then name the smallest synchronization boundary that preserves correctness. Do not write code yet.

prompts.label: Tests that expose bugs
prompts.text: Suggest tests that could expose bugs in my implementation: boundaries, duplicates, empty and invalid input, and concurrency where it applies. For each, say why the expected value is correct.

prompts.label: Complexity check
prompts.text: What is the time and space complexity of each public method as written? Do not claim a bound unless every step achieves it.

prompts.label: Requirement change
prompts.text: The requirement changed: Add ThreeSum.Closest(nums, target) (long); ties go to the smaller sum; fewer than three numbers → ArgumentException. List which members need to change and which do not, before writing any code.

learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: Return every **unique** triplet `(a, b, c)` from the array with `a + b + c == 0`. Each triplet ascending; the list in ascending order.

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Unique by value, not by index? (By value.)
- Can I sort a copy? (Yes; do not reorder the input.)
- Can the sum overflow int? (Use long.)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: Fixing one element turns 3Sum into 2Sum on a sorted suffix, which two pointers solve in linear time. Duplicates are skipped by moving past equal neighbours — at the anchor and after every hit.

learn.title: 4 · Approach
learn.md: I would say, before coding: "S."ort once, fix the first element, and close two pointers from both ends of the rest — O(n²) with duplicates skipped at every pointer so each triplet is produced once."

learn.title: 10 · Tests
learn.md:
**S1 — Zero-sum triplets**

- [-1,0,1,2,-1,-4]
- [0,0,0,0]
- none
- large values do not overflow
- input not reordered
- 3,000 values in … ms (< 1500 — O(n^2))

**S2 — Closest to a target**

- [-1,2,1,-4], 1
- [0,0,0], 1
- tie goes to the smaller sum
- two numbers

learn.title: 11 · AI usage strategy
learn.md:

- Delegate the mechanical parts only after the structure is fixed.

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- Using a HashSet of triplets to dedupe (works, but hides an O(n² log n) and allocation).
- Skipping duplicates only at the anchor.
- int overflow on three large values.
- O(n³) brute force.
